events.summary: A core team member opens the Layouts RFC: nested layouts in a new app directory, built for Server Components, parallel data fetching, React 18 features and incremental adoption; the post was later edited to point to an update.
A user praises the RFC but questions the page.js name, since a nested segment is really a component rather than a page.
A user asks why not keep underscore-prefixed names like _page.js and _layout.js.
A user asks whether TypeScript extensions are accepted for page files.
A core team member confirms js, jsx, ts and tsx all work.
A contributor asks how optional catch-all routes work with page.js.
A user asks how layouts behave in catch-all folders, about intercepting routes, and how server and client components are detected.
A user warns of hundreds of identically named page files and proposes name-prefixed files like home.page.tsx and home.layout.tsx.
A user questions page.tsx naming, suggests an underscore prefix or a config option, and asks about role-based layouts.
A user asks whether getInitialProps will still work with layouts for client-side caches.
A user agrees page.js is repetitive and suggests a single special-character prefix, with an editor screenshot.
A React core member notes an alternative server/client file convention is being discussed in the React RFC.
A contributor asks whether fetching data directly in server components or via getServerSideProps is the intended approach.
A contributor prefers a file-per-route scheme with settings.layout.js and an optional folder for children, avoiding renames into page.js.
A user asks the docs to clarify that page refers to the file name, not only the .js extension.
A user asks about error boundaries per layout.
A core team member agrees to fix the wording.
A user asks how committed the team is to the app directory name and proposes routes, citing monorepo apps folders.
A user asks how a parent route could fetch shared data once for nested routes instead of every segment refetching.
A contributor asks how pages and app coexist, about error pages per segment, layouts without pages, and worries about tying layouts to unreleased Server Components.
A user asks how a layout could pass props to its page if it only receives children.
A user asks for a release estimate.
A user asks how to share one layout across separate URL segments.
A user suggests importing a shared layout component into each layout file, or moving the layout higher.
A contributor notes many projects already use an app folder for application code and suggests routes instead.
A user proposes keeping route names as files with only an underscore-prefixed layout file.
A React core member says getInitialProps will likely remain for compatibility and data seeding is being explored.
A user strongly prefers routes over app because app often holds business logic.
A user agrees with the naming concern and asks for dashboard.page.js style names.
A user asks for Remix-style pathless layout routes so folders need not become URL segments.
A contributor asks whether a child route can opt out of parent layouts, citing embedded widget pages.
A user agrees an underscore-prefixed route file would ease colocation.
A user adds that a landing page often needs to escape the shared layout.
A user suggests making the app folder name configurable.
A user suggests underscore-prefixed files could be excluded from routing.
A user describes the pain of many index.js files and supports type-suffixed names.
A contributor prefers route.js and a routes directory and shares a draft RFC for routes directories with colocation.
A user asks whether data can be fetched at component level.
A maintainer asks what happens to pages/api and middleware.
A user supports a configurable directory name for projects with an existing app folder.
A user agrees with type-suffixed names.
The maintainer notes middleware is moving to the root anyway.
A contributor says the docs wording should reflect configurable page extensions.
A user describes JWT refresh handling and worries every segment's data function would repeat it.
A user agrees with the naming concern.
A contributor outlines handling auth refresh in parallel loading via a layout-issued redirect.
A user asks for glob-based on-demand revalidation now that layouts fetch data.
A user asks how a nested page can have an entirely different layout.
A user asks what server-centric routing with SPA-like behaviour means.
A user votes for pathless layouts with an admin-section example.
A user asks how CMS-controlled URLs handled by catch-all routes fit folder-defined layouts.
A user asks whether data fetched in a parent layout can be shared with nested routes.
A core team member says dynamic segments remain supported as folder names.
A core team member explains data fetching outside the tree avoids waterfalls for now, with in-component fetching supported later.
A core team member answers that app wins on conflicts, pages stays for incremental migration, layouts without pages are allowed, and Server Components are close.
A core team member says folders outside the URL will be covered in part two.
A core team member says opting out of parent layouts will be covered in part two.
A core team member says this will be covered in part two.
A core team member explains server-rendered components applied on the client.
A user asks whether root-layout data fetching avoids refetching on navigation.
A core team member says the root layout persists so its data is not refetched on client navigation.
A user hoped app would allow Blitz-style colocation.
A user adds support.
The user realises colocation is already covered.
A user asks for nested error boundaries and Remix-style form actions.
A user asks whether offscreen stashing enables app-like back and forward.
A core team member says new apps will use app by default and pages will be deprecated only over a very long horizon.
A contributor asks whether component-level Suspense can replace getServerSideProps and how to read params.
A user worries nested layouts couple layout to URL structure when paths are organised differently.
A core team member says no date yet but several team members have worked on it for months.
A user asks about next export support.
A user proposes named slots in layouts so routes can override parts like headers.
A user shares the coupling concern and asks to keep the flexible getLayout pattern.
A user asks whether wrapper was considered instead of layout as the name.
A contributor agrees wrapper would be more general.
A contributor agrees app is a poor choice because projects already use it for application files.
A core team member explains folders with fixed file names enable colocation of tests and styles, clear layout nesting, and further conventions like loading.js.
A user asks whether IE11 support is dropped.
A user asks whether static generation remains possible.
A team member says Server Components do not force per-request SSR and routes can still be static.
A team member says context will handle passing data from layout to page.
A team member points to an earlier answer.
A user suggests routes as the default with a configurable name.
A contributor strongly prefers routes because thousands of Blitz apps already use app.
A user asks why app was chosen and asks for it to be configurable from the start.
A user asks for a release date.
A user asks for translated URL segments for i18n.
A contributor suggests per-folder package.json main fields or a config mapper so route files can have descriptive names.
A contributor says needing such workarounds signals a problem in the core API.
A user is eager for the release.
A user calls the app folder name confusing and asks for route.
A user supports route names in file names with short type suffixes.
A user enthusiastically supports the RFC.
A team member answers that some static sub-layouts under dynamic layouts cannot stay fully static.
A user asks whether modal routes can use static generation.
A user argues editors already let you search by folder path, so repeated names are manageable.
A user asks whether the RFC is in any release yet.
A core team member says not yet.
A user asks for a date.
A contributor shows identical names also hurt error traces, React DevTools and editor tabs.
A user wishes for optional config-file routing and asks about sharing layouts across sibling routes.
A user asks to move API routes out of pages.
A React core member says DevTools could show the folder name for such files.
A user objects to abbreviated type suffixes as hard to read.
A user asks for more naming variants than page.jsx, arguing quick navigation becomes useless.
A user argues reading the parent folder name is easy and folder names have clear advantages.
A user asks whether it lands in Next.js 13.
A user asks for an alternative to next/head for streaming.
A core team member says a preview will be released before Next.js 13.
A user asks whether CSS can be imported at layout level.
A user asks about programmatically adding routes via config.
A user asks when it will roll out.
A user asks whether part two is still coming.
A user asks for custom per-language paths.
A user asks how this affects a Relay setup.
A user asks to rename or configure the app directory, preferring routes.
A user asks whether it is available in 12.2.
A user asks when it will roll out.
A user asks how to be notified of a canary.
A user asks for updates.
A user asks how getStaticProps interacts with server components.
A core team member links a progress update posted on social media.
A user asks how to give different groups of pages entirely different main layouts.
A core team member previews route groups using parenthesised folders that do not affect the URL, allowing separate layouts and multiple root layouts.
The core team member notes a typo in the example.
A user likes route groups but still dislikes repeated page.js files and proposes _layout.js with route-named files.
A user asks for an ETA and notes part two is missing.
A user asks for patience.
A user prefers directory routing over config-based routing.
A user says Next.js may not suit everyone.
A user asks for a release date.
A user looks forward to better nested routing.
A user asks what replaces the pages folder and API routes.
A user asks for a rough timeframe.
A user asks for typed routes instead of loosely defined file-system routes.
A user asks for a release date.
A user predicts a reveal at the Next.js conference and links the part-two update in the 12.3 blog post.
A user asks whether part two exists.
A user links the part-two update.
A user notes the page.js naming concern remains unchanged in part two and asks whether an alternative scheme is still possible or the naming is final.
The user says index.js would not fix repeated names.
The user repeats the earlier screenshot illustrating repeated names.
A contributor backs type-suffixed names like name.page.js and prefers routes over app.
A contributor notes intercepting routes suit modal-over-feed patterns.
A user asks to move the api folder out of pages.
A contributor says the intercepting-route DX looks tedious for globally available modals.
A contributor asks whether custom servers will support Server Components.
A user asks for an example with a src folder.
A user asks again how CMS-owned URLs fit folder-defined layouts.

A core team member says he hid two off-topic comments and points to the conference.
